item.title: Accuracy of the Epicycle Model for Predicting Eclipses
item.description: Over 2,000 years ago, the Greek astronomer Hipparchus (c. 150 BC) developed one of the first geometric models to predict the motion of the Sun and Moon. In this model, the Moon moves on a small circle called the epicycle, which itself moves on a larger circle called the deferent. Both these motions are uniform. The main reason for introducing this model was to explain the observed non-uniform motion. The ancient Babylonian astronomers had noticed that the moon sometimes moved faster across the sky than at other times.

item.title: Slicing Circles: How Kepler Solved Planetary Motion
item.description: Suppose we want to slice a given circle into two segments using a chord. If our goal is to divide the circle so that the areas of the two segments have a specified ratio, where along the diameter should we make the cut? Conceptually, this is not a very difficult geometric problem. Let the circle have radius $r=1$ (a unit circle), and let $x$ be the distance from the center to the cut.
